scope: Read-only G0/G1 environment semantic audit before G2; no neural training or full G0 rerun; frozen sources unchanged.
conclusion: Normal step-path semantics support proceeding to G2 preparation. No observed finding invalidates the reported G0 mechanism counts. Correct the verified state-load finite-value gap and make the PPO collector contract explicit before training/resume.
verified_behaviors: Current/best/anchor are separate and proposals are independently certified before bounded acceptance.
Quality reward uses best-so-far improvement and final fallback correction; unchanged and failed proposals are charged.
STOP, horizon and work-budget endings inside step are true terminal states. Collector boundary preserves nonterminal state and bootstrap.
rollout_record stores exact sampled action order, mask, chosen action and finite sampled log probability/value, and rejects mismatch with step info.
Shared menu construction never calls the exact repair solver; repair proposer explicitly forbids only the one removed candidate for replace.
Immutable F, arm_dist and D are created from immutable byte buffers; input source/problem are deep-copied.

findings.title: External termination events are not PPO transitions
findings.nature: Known event-based runtime design; not a defect in the audited G0 totals, which include events. It becomes a training bug if a collector uses transitions alone.
findings.evidence: Minimal fixture: default step reward=-0.005, external termination reward=-0.002, complete return=-0.007. With potential_weight=.4, step reward=-.405 and terminal event=+.398, complete return=-.007. The stored prior transition remains terminated=False.
findings.correction: For the first PPO version use only step-driven horizon/work/STOP true terminals and collector truncations for batch cuts. If external deadlines/finalize are used in training, merge terminal event reward into the final transition, update terminal observation and terminated=True, and disable bootstrap. Zero-action runtime termination produces an episode metric but no actor sample.
findings.blocking: Blocks a PPO collector that ignores external events; does not block one explicitly limited to step-driven terminals.

findings.title: load_state_dict accepts NaN costs and totals
findings.nature: Verified validation gap in checkpoint restoration; clean saved G0 data were not shown to contain NaN.
findings.evidence: Injecting NaN into each of anchor_cost/current_cost/best_cost in an otherwise valid synthetic state is accepted; the next step returns nonfinite reward. NaN total_reward is also accepted. abs(nan)>tolerance evaluates False.
findings.correction: Validate every stored cost/return/shaping/penalty/timing numeric as finite before comparisons; costs nonnegative, steps/work integer and nonnegative; assert best_cost<=current_cost and best_cost<=anchor_cost, current acceptance bound, and termination/horizon/work/returned-certificate consistency. Validate menu/config identity before exposing restored observation. Reject malformed state before mutating env.
findings.blocking: Fix before enabling resumable training/checkpoint restoration. It is not evidence that ordinary current runs are corrupt.

findings.title: Current observe output is not the proposed graph-policy input
findings.nature: Explicit G1 scope boundary, not an implementation bug.
findings.evidence: Observation includes 22 scalar action features, route/costs and task coverage counts, but no F/D/candidate geometry. Per-action required-task/pool/retained lists remain in menu diagnostics, outside observe. The report does not claim this observation is a sufficient Markov representation.
findings.correction: Create an immutable scene graph registry keyed by problem_id and feature schema/hash, supply F or its valid route-level union, navigation D, service attributes and dynamic route/coverage/best/budget context. Persist sufficient raw graph/ordered menu identifiers for PPO recomputation. Treat the 22-feature shared MLP as a compact baseline, not automatically a graph policy.
findings.blocking: Required to implement the proposed graph actor-critic; existing environment can be reused.

findings.title: Replay context hashes cannot serve as semantic repeated-query keys
findings.nature: Disclosed interface-reference limitation, not concealed strong baseline.
findings.evidence: Action key includes remaining budget, step count and the full prior history. The same route/operator/window query gets a different key every step. Greedy has no repeat handling; adaptive reference rewards every accepted feasible move with 1, including no-change proposals.
findings.correction: Separate replay identity from proposal identity: use problem+full route+operator/window/forbidden node+solver caps for deterministic repeated-query detection. Store outcome/changed flags. Share any no-op/failed-query suppression and menu refill/cap rules across PPO, BC and rule baselines. Tune a stronger rule baseline on development scenes and report no-change reward/acceptance handling explicitly.
findings.blocking: Must fix or explicitly control before claiming PPO beats a strong same-action rule. Does not invalidate G0 search-tree evidence.

disclosed_tradeoff_not_bug.menu_work: step eagerly constructs the next observation/menu; menu work is charged on the next step or terminate event. This is a documented soft budget, and pending_menu_work/work_after_menu expose it. Future lazy/stop-before-menu optimization must get a new protocol and shared baseline treatment, not alter old records.
disclosed_tradeoff_not_bug.timing: Work units are deterministic proxies, not FLOPs or CPU shares. Complete scene-to-plan timing remains necessary.

actual_actions: Read rl_env.py, action_builder.py, repair_proposal.py, adapter.py, policies.py, runtime_rl.py, types.py, test_env.py.
Ran only short synthetic fixture reproductions for malformed-state loading and external terminal-event accounting.
No source code modification, no policy training, no full G0 rerun.
